amy-howorth.text: Seconded the July 2026 motion, passed 5-0, advancing a restructured business license tax (Model 4) toward the November ballot with a $100,000 cap; opposed lowering the cap, saying businesses reaching it are the city's biggest. Pushed to end the exemption for independent real estate agents.

source.title: City Finance: Council moves towards business tax ballot measure - Easy Reader (Jul 24, 2026)

amy-howorth.text: Seconded and voted for the April 2026 six-month electric microtransit pilot (3-1-1): "We have a fiduciary responsibility to try the pilot," citing Dial-a-Ride's roughly $145-per-ride cost.

source.title: City Council: Low-cost electric microtransit program approved - Easy Reader (Apr 9, 2026)

amy-howorth.text: On the downtown Project Pulse concept, opposed second-floor creative office space and a 4,100 sq. ft. retail space that would attract "a national brand": "When people talk about small town feel, they're talking about small local businesses."

source.title: Manhattan Beach contemplates Project Pulse, a major downtown overhaul - Easy Reader (Sep 19, 2026)

amy-howorth.text: Pressed staff in April 2026 on whether added downtown parking was actually used, and pushed for merchant parking permit increases to be phased in gradually.

source.title: City Council: Manhattan Beach parking study shows big shortage - Easy Reader (Apr 16, 2026)

amy-howorth.text: (2023) With Councilmember Lesser, put a formal Bruce's Beach apology back on the agenda; it passed 4-1: "they were wrong. We have a chance to correct the course for our city."

source.title: City Council issues a formal Bruce's Beach apology - Easy Reader (Apr 6, 2023)

amy-howorth.text: (2023) On misdemeanor non-prosecution, said Prop 47's reclassification of felonies to misdemeanors is "part of the problem, too... it's sort of like a catch and release."

source.title: Public Safety: City seeks to evade DA block on misdemeanor prosecution - Easy Reader (Jun 30, 2023)

richard-p-montgomery.text: At the September 2026 Project Pulse hearing, urged the council to put both downtown properties out to private developers: "Get out of the way... Don't spend any more money. No more staff time."

source.title: Manhattan Beach contemplates Project Pulse, a major downtown overhaul - Easy Reader (Sep 19, 2026)

richard-p-montgomery.text: (2023) As mayor, on misdemeanor prosecution: "Public safety is number one"; backed the city exploring its own prosecution: "I don't believe the pie-in-the-sky unicorn stuff that's out there."

source.title: Public Safety: City seeks to evade DA block on misdemeanor prosecution - Easy Reader (Jun 30, 2023)

richard-p-montgomery.text: (2023) Voted for the 4-1 formal apology for Bruce's Beach: "We are an anti-racist city." Had called for an apology in 2006.

source.title: City Council issues a formal Bruce's Beach apology - Easy Reader (Apr 6, 2023)

richard-p-montgomery.text: (2024) In farewell remarks as he termed out, pointed to rebuilding Fire Station #2, the Polliwog playground and Peck Reservoir among council accomplishments: "It was a team effort."

source.title: Manhattan City Council: Napolitano, Montgomery bow out - Easy Reader (Dec 21, 2024)

mark-burton.text: 2026 letter: running to put residents first, with "a proven record of fighting to ensure city business was conducted with absolute transparency" and "demanding fiscal accountability that reduces wasteful spending."

source.title: Letters to the Editor 08-20-26 (Mark Burton, 'Round two') - Easy Reader

mark-burton.text: Urged a city hiring freeze instead of higher fees and taxes, noting full-time staff grew from 268 to 357; said cutting 30 positions would save $7 million or more.

source.title: Letters, June 12, 2026 (Mark Burton, 'Let city heads roll back') - Easy Reader

mark-burton.text: Faulted the council for saying its hands are tied on high-rise apartments; urged lobbying to exempt small dense cities from Density Bonus Law height waivers and adopting criteria to deny waivers on health or safety grounds.

source.title: Letters to the Editor (Mark Burton, 'Do nothing party') - Easy Reader (Apr 8, 2026)

mark-burton.text: (2024) Opposed the city's pension obligation bonds and noted the city sought a half-cent sales tax; urged council members willing to cut full-time staff and control salaries.

source.title: Letters to the Editor 10-10-24 (Mark Burton) - Easy Reader

mark-burton.text: (2024) Urged voters to elect council members who would "reduce staffing and salaries," citing $80 million in pension debt.

source.title: Letters to the Editor 10-31-24 (Mark Burton, 'Freshen up') - Easy Reader

mark-burton.text: (2024) Supported MBUSD school bond Measure RLS, noting it maintained the current tax rate and could draw $57 million in state matching funds.

source.title: Letters to the Editor 9-19-24 (Mark Burton, 'Cornerstone schools') - Easy Reader

mark-burton.text: (2024) Called DA Gascon's misdemeanor policy "reckless" and urged Manhattan Beach to explore a city charter to hire its own city prosecutor.

source.title: Letters to the Editor 9-5-24 (Mark Burton, 'Crime free charter') - Easy Reader

joseph-ungoco.text: (2019) Ran as "the sustainability candidate," urging green-building incentives in local building codes and better infrastructure for multi-modal transportation.

source.title: Ungoco argues for sustainability and fresh perspective - Easy Reader (Mar 2, 2019)

joseph-ungoco.text: (2019) Argued newer residents deserve representation: "The past of Manhattan Beach is very well guarded on our council. The future is not represented."

source.title: Ungoco argues for sustainability and fresh perspective - Easy Reader (Mar 2, 2019)

notes: Howorth (incumbent) evidence from 2026 Easy Reader council coverage plus 2023 votes; Montgomery mostly from his prior council tenure; Burton from his own Easy Reader letters. Ungoco (Planning Commission vice-chair) has only 2019 campaign statements findable; Beach Reporter/MB News and city clerk pages blocked fetching. Searches used: 10
